summary.headline: Runtime state and history persistence contain inconsistencies.

findings.title: agents.yaml reports running panes whose recorded PIDs no longer exist

evidence.detail: pane-72, pane-73, and pane-74 are marked status=running with recorded PIDs 559748, 567291, and 680856
No matching live processes were returned

findings.impact: Consumers of runtime state may believe panes are still active and make incorrect UI or orchestration decisions.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Investigate pane exit handling and stale runtime-state cleanup.

findings.title: sessions.json contains duplicate session IDs

evidence.detail: Multiple identical session IDs appear more than once with slightly different endedAt and totalDurationMs values

findings.impact: Session lists and aggregates can double count or display duplicate history rows.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Check session finalization and index append logic for idempotency.

findings.title: A recent history directory contains turns without session metadata

evidence.detail: Directory contains many turn-*.json files but no session.json

findings.impact: History replay and session-level inspection can fail or become partial after interrupted writes.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Review ordering and durability guarantees between turn persistence and session metadata persistence.

findings.title: Long-lived panes are configured to share the same workspace

evidence.detail: pane-72, pane-73, and pane-74 are configured with isolation=shared
The workspace already contains uncommitted changes

findings.impact: Concurrent agents can interfere with each other's assumptions and edits in the shared worktree.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Prefer isolated worktrees for long-running or overlapping tasks when coordination is weak.

activity_notes.note: Observed creation of a documentation design spec and subsequent transition to idle.
Observed prompt interaction and a SKILL.md read, with no file edit activity in inspected turns.
